# 🔴 PARTIAL, HAND-SEEDED LIST — not generated by running extract-files.py against a
# rooted device (that requires a synced LineageOS 23 source tree, which we don't have yet).
# Every path below was directly confirmed present on Jelly Star via live `adb shell find`/
# `/proc/<pid>/maps` inspection during this session's NFC and BT-A2DP debugging (2026-09-28
# and 2026-09-29) — real evidence, not guessed. This is NOT the complete blob list a real
# device port needs (camera, sensors, RIL, GPU userspace, etc. are not covered at all yet)
# — it's a documented head start on the two subsystems this port's diagnostics focused on.
# Run `./extract-files.py --adb` once a LineageOS 23 tree exists around this device tree to
# generate the real, complete list (per iKKO's own documented workflow, docs/BLOBS.md) —
# that process will supersede this hand-seeded file, not just append to it.

# NFC (TMS chip) — the SystemServer-never-starts-NfcService bug's target. HAL binary/libs
# themselves are not actually the bug (see memory: SystemServer never attempts to start the
# service at all, so these blobs being present isn't sufficient by itself) but are needed
# regardless for the HAL side to function once the framework-side fix is in place.
vendor/bin/hw/android.hardware.nfc-service-tms
vendor/etc/init/nfc-service-tms.rc
vendor/etc/libnfc-tms.conf
vendor/etc/libnfc-tms_RF.conf
vendor/etc/libnfc-tms_RF_EC2.conf
vendor/etc/libnfc-tms_RF_GB1.conf
vendor/etc/libnfc-tms_RF_GC2.conf
vendor/etc/vintf/manifest/nfc-service-tms.xml
# REMOVED (collides with source-buildable AOSP/hardware-mediatek module, 2026-09-29): vendor/lib/android.hardware.nfc@1.0.so
vendor/lib/vendor.tms.tmsnfc_aidl-V1-ndk.so
# android.hardware.nfc-V1-ndk.so: NOT extracted as a blob — standard AOSP AIDL interface
# library, buildable from source in hardware/interfaces/nfc/aidl/. Extracting it as a
# prebuilt collided with the source-built one (Soong "partition is different" error,
# 2026-09-29 first build attempt) since our device tree's copy defaulted to vendor
# partition while AOSP's source-built one is system partition.
# REMOVED (collides with source-buildable AOSP/hardware-mediatek module, 2026-09-29): vendor/lib64/android.hardware.nfc@1.0.so
vendor/lib64/nfc_nci.thn31nfc.tms.so
vendor/lib64/vendor.tms.tmsnfc_aidl-V1-ndk.so

# Audio — the AUDIO_FORMAT_APTX/DeviceDescriptor=NULL bug's target (framework-side, but the
# HAL config files below are exactly where the confirmed fix — adding an APTX <profile>
# entry to the "bluetooth" module's a2dp mixPort — needs to land as a device-tree override).

vendor/etc/audio_policy.conf
# 🔴 audio_policy_configuration.xml and bluetooth_audio_policy_configuration.xml: extract
# the STOCK versions here for reference/diffing, but the device tree will need its OWN
# override copy of at least the bluetooth one (via PRODUCT_COPY_FILES in device.mk) with
# the APTX profile fix added — do not just symlink the stock blob once that fix is written.
vendor/etc/audio_policy_configuration.xml
vendor/etc/audio_policy_configuration_bluetooth_legacy_hal.xml
vendor/etc/audio_policy_volumes.xml

# device/unihertz/jellystar/audio/bluetooth_audio_policy_configuration.xml, wired via
# PRODUCT_COPY_FILES in device.mk -- adds the AUDIO_FORMAT_APTX <profile> entry confirmed
# (via Frida) to be the actual fix for the BT A2DP bug this port exists to solve. See the
# comment header in that file for the full root-cause writeup.
# vendor/etc/bluetooth_audio_policy_configuration.xml

# Renamed on install (2026-09-30): the real stock filename "bluetooth_audio.xml" collides
# with hardware/interfaces/bluetooth/audio/aidl/default's own same-named generic reference
# fragment (same class of collision as android.hardware.audio.service-aidl.xml, fixed the
# same way — rename since VINTF only cares about content, not filename).

# Renamed on install (2026-09-30): these 4 plain names exactly match hardware/interfaces/
# bluetooth/audio/utils/Android.bp's own `required:` list of prebuilt_etc modules (a real
# AOSP source module, same collision class as android.hardware.audio.service-aidl.xml and
# bluetooth_audio.xml above) — renamed with a ".mediatek" tag to disambiguate from AOSP's
# own copies. The "_mtk" suffixed siblings alongside these are untouched, separate files.
vendor/etc/aidl/le_audio/aidl_audio_set_configurations.bfbs:vendor/etc/aidl/le_audio/aidl_audio_set_configurations.mediatek.bfbs

vendor/etc/aidl/le_audio/aidl_default_audio_set_configurations.json_mtk
vendor/etc/aidl/le_audio/aidl_default_audio_set_scenarios.json:vendor/etc/aidl/le_audio/aidl_default_audio_set_scenarios.mediatek.json

# IMS (VoLTE) - from stock V01.00.04 system_ext. ImsService (com.mediatek.ims, android.uid.phone) is
# re-signed with the platform key; its only MediaTek dependency is mediatek-ims-base, which goes
# on the boot classpath (PRODUCT_BOOT_JARS in device.mk). The video telephony libraries are loaded
# by ImsService at startup (libmtk_vt_wrapper), so they are required even without video calls.
# libsink is renamed: it clashes with a Rust module of the same name.
system_ext/framework/mediatek-ims-base.jar:system/framework/mediatek-ims-base.jar
system_ext/priv-app/ImsService/ImsService.apk
system_ext/lib64/libcomutils.so

system_ext/lib64/libmtk_vt_service.so
system_ext/lib64/libmtk_vt_wrapper.so
system_ext/lib64/libsignal.so
system_ext/lib64/libsink.so:system_ext/lib64/libsink-mtk.so
system_ext/lib64/libsource.so
system_ext/lib64/libvcodec_cap.so
system_ext/lib64/libvcodec_capenc.so
system_ext/lib64/libvt_avsync.so
